evidence.source: Shuowen.cn, digitized 說文解字 and 段玉裁注
evidence.text: The entry gives 气 as “雲气也。象形” (cloud vapor; pictograph). Duan Yucai’s note says 气 and 氣 were ancient/current forms, that 氣 came to be used for cloud vapor, and 餼 was then made for the grain-gift sense. This is a traditional lexicographic account, not independent confirmation of the graph’s earliest referent.

evidence.source: CASE 報科學, specialist paleography discussion
evidence.text: The article reports oracle-bone forms of 气 as three strokes, distinguishes the graph 气 from the later small-seal 氣, and reviews competing readings. It cites instances such as 合12532 and 粹771 as proposed cloud/rain uses, but argues that no known oracle-bone context securely uses 气 as a noun meaning cloud vapor. Other proposed interpretations include a “cut/sever” graph, and readings connected with 迄 or 訖; the article records disagreement over how to segment 气至 in 合6057. It concludes that the oracle-bone referent remains unresolved. No glyph image was visually inspected for this report.
evidence.title: 甲骨文的「云」與「气」

evidence.field: 氣 entry, as quoted in the 氣 dictionary entry
evidence.text: Shuowen analyzes 氣 as “饋客芻米也。从米气聲” (fodder and grain supplied to a guest; from 米, with 气 as phonetic), and cites 春秋傳 “齊人來氣諸矦.” This supports 米 as semantic and 气 as phonetic in Shuowen’s analysis of 氣; the cited passage is a dictionary quotation and does not by itself date the graph’s creation.
evidence.title: 氣说文解字原文

evidence.source: 教育百科, Ministry of Education of Taiwan educational dictionary
evidence.field: 氣 senses and cited early textual uses
evidence.text: The entry distinguishes 氣 read xì, “grain supplied to a guest,” citing Shuowen and 春秋傳, from qì senses. For qì it cites the Zhuangzi phrase 雲氣不待族而雨 for cloud vapor and Zuǒzhuàn 昭公元年 “天有六氣” for the six atmospheric conditions, traditionally glossed as yin, yang, wind, rain, darkness, and brightness. These citations attest textual uses, but the dictionary does not establish the dates of the underlying textual layers or a precise semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 氣 的意思、注音與解釋

evidence.source: 中國哲學書電子化計劃, 康熙字典
evidence.field: 氣 entry; historical readings and glosses
evidence.text: The Kangxi entry preserves separate sound-and-sense traditions: 去既切 for the ordinary breath/air-related reading, and 許既切 with the Shuowen gloss “饋客芻米也” for the food-gift sense, also noting later association with 餼. It compiles earlier authorities and is not itself an early attestation.
evidence.title: 康熙字典 : 气部 : 六

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart 2014 readings supplied in local table and cross-checked against opened Wiktionary character page
evidence.text: The supplied local Baxter–Sagart table gives 气 qì, MC khj+jH, OC *C.qʰəp-s; and 氣 qì, MC khj+jH, OC *C.qʰəp-s (cloudy vapors), plus 氣 xì, MC xj+jH, OC *qʰət-s (to present food). The opened character page reproduces these distinctions and labels its notation Baxter–Sagart system 1.1 (2014). Local rows were checked exactly; the page is secondary transcription, not the source of the local table. The xì reading is a separate lexical reading and should not be merged with the qì reading.

evidence.source: Wiktionary character entry, citing Baxter–Sagart 2014 and Zhengzhang Shangfang 2003
evidence.field: 氣 qì and xì phonological entries
evidence.text: For 氣 qì, the page gives Middle Chinese Baxter khj+jH, fanqie 去既, OC Baxter–Sagart *C.qʰəp-s and Zhengzhang *kʰɯds. For 氣 xì, it gives MC Baxter xj+jH, fanqie 許既, OC Baxter–Sagart *qʰət-s and Zhengzhang *qʰɯds. These are different reconstruction systems and lexical readings, not interchangeable transcriptions. The local Baxter–Sagart table agrees with the page’s B–S forms for 氣.
evidence.title: 氣 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary character entry, Zhengzhang Shangfang reconstruction data
evidence.field: 气 as phonetic component under 氣 readings
evidence.text: For 氣, the page identifies 气 as the phonetic component and lists Zhengzhang OC *kʰɯds under the qì reading and *qʰɯds under xì. The retrieved material did not expose a separate character-specific modern or historical reading table for 气 adequate to independently verify its Zhengzhang reconstruction; do not assume the host’s value is automatically the component’s value. The provided Baxter–Sagart local 气 row is *C.qʰəp-s, matching the supplied 氣 qì row, while 氣 xì is *qʰət-s; that supports a proposed phonetic relationship for the qì entry within this system but does not establish the sound history or reading of the graph’s original depicted referent.
evidence.title: 氣 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: 国务院, 1956 汉字简化方案 as reproduced by Wikisource
evidence.field: First simplified-character table and adoption date
evidence.text: The 1956 scheme identifies 气（氣） in its first list of simplified characters, and states that the first-list forms were to be used generally from 1956-02-01. This documents 气 as the standardized simplified counterpart of 氣 in that scheme; it does not imply that the 气 graph originated in 1956, since older 气 forms are separately reported in paleographic sources.
evidence.title: 汉字简化方案

evidence.text: The page lists a 气 specimen labeled 前7.36.2 (甲), followed by early Western Zhou bronze 天亡簋, late Spring and Autumn bronze 洹子孟姜壺, Chu manuscript examples, the Shuowen seal form, Qin clerical manuscript specimens, Western Han 老子乙, Eastern Han 魯峻碑, and regular script. The labels provide an available sequence of examples but the page does not provide a detailed palaeographic argument for each form, and no images were visually inspected here.

gaps: The direct official Unihan records for U+6C14 and U+6C23 were attempted multiple times and inaccessible. The harness-supplied local kMandarin rows were checked and agree at qì, but the requested official per-character click-through could not be verified.

The local Baxter–Sagart rows were checked exactly: 气 qì MC khj+jH OC *C.qʰəp-s; 氣 qì MC khj+jH OC *C.qʰəp-s; 氣 xì MC xj+jH OC *qʰət-s. No separate component-specific Zhengzhang 气 row was retrieved, so do not reuse 氣’s reconstructed value as if independently attested for 气.

Oracle-bone 气 is reported in examples, but its earliest graphic referent and whether the cited contexts mean cloud vapor, cut/sever, or a phonetic loan for 迄/訖 remain disputed. Claims that its original strokes depict vapor or heat waves are not established by the inspected primary/specialist evidence.

The chronological and semantic transition between 气, 氣, and 餼 is presented differently in traditional lexicography and modern specialist discussion. The inspected evidence does not settle when the qì breath/air sense began to be written with 氣 or precisely how sense extensions proceeded.

The old-text citations to 春秋傳, Zhuangzi, and Zuǒzhuàn昭公元年 are reported through dictionary entries; textual layer dates and the earliest securely dated attestation for each sense were not established here.
No image was visually inspected. The Shuowen.cn specimen sequence is a page index, not a visual verification or independent palaeographic collation.

Unihan is a recurring source in this project, but no exact license grant for reproducing extracts was verified. Do not infer bulk-reuse permission from its public lookup interface; no tracked extract recommendation is made.
